title: Graceful degradation and transparent Retry headers after 429 burst (quota enforcer grace-window misfire)
creator: Priya Nair
description: After a production surge on 2026-02-28 we observed a sustained spike in 429 responses from the API gateway lasting ~90 minutes. This ticket captures the investigation summary, root cause, corrective fixes, and follow-up action items to prevent recurrence. The dominant customer-facing problem was a large cohort of legitimate requests getting hard-failed (429) instead of being routed to degraded but operational paths or receiving transparent Retry-After guidance.
timeline: 2026-02-28T08:54Z - Ops alert: 429 rate > 5% baseline for gateway-proxy in us-east-1
2026-02-28T09:02Z - Pager duty fired; incident declared: GATEWAY-429-BURST
2026-02-28T09:10Z - Mitigation: temporarily increased per-token burst window for tiered customers; partial reduction in 429s
2026-02-28T10:05Z - Root cause hypothesis formed: grace-window evaluation returning false for renewed tokens
2026-02-28T11:30Z - Hotfix deployed to restore correct TTL units and short-circuit enforcement for in-flight auth cache refreshes
2026-02-28T12:05Z - 429s returned to baseline; incident closed as mitigated with follow-ups assigned
root_cause: Race and unit bug: recent change to the auth cache refresh logic (PR #4021) introduced a TTL normalization bug where grace-window values returned by the auth service were interpreted as milliseconds instead of seconds in the quota enforcer path. In high churn (many token renewals) this caused the grace-window check to evaluate to expired immediately for a shard subset. Combined with a change that tightened enforcer fallback (hard enforcement when grace-window mismatch detected), a large fraction of valid requests were counted against quota and turned into 429s.
observations: The error surface was concentrated on 3 of 12 gateway shards (consistent with shard-dependent TTL parsing path), explaining partial regional impact
Alert rules only counted absolute 429 volume; we lacked a specific alert for sudden increase in Retry-After-less 429s
No metric existed for 'grace-window-hit' or 'grace-window-mismatch' counters prior to the incident
SDKs and a fraction of clients ignore Retry-After headers; without transparent headers some clients retried aggressively causing secondary load
action_items: ENG-66011.1: Fix TTL normalization bug in quota enforcer (patch merged; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/5198) - owner: Ben Howard - estimate: 2
ENG-66011.2: Add unit + integration tests covering TTL units and race scenarios with concurrent auth cache refresh - owner: Aisha Khan - estimate: 3
ENG-66011.3: Add 'grace_window_mismatch' and 'grace_window_hit' metrics with per-shard granularity; expose in Console per-route dashboard - owner: Marcelo Vega - estimate: 3

ENG-66011.4: Implement transparent Retry headers (Retry-After + X-Redwood-Retryable: true/false) so clients can make informed backoff decisions; coordinate SDK teams for patch rollout - owner: Priya Nair - estimate: 5
ENG-66011.5: Canary rollout plan with automatic rollback trigger if 429s or error-rate increase > 3% over baseline within 30m - owner: Ben Howard - estimate: 2
ENG-66011.6: Create an incident playbook section for 'grace-window' and 'quota-enforcer' failures and run a simulated fire drill in March cycle - owner: On-call rotation lead - estimate: 1
ENG-66011.7: Post-deploy dashboard card that surfaces Retry-After-less 429s and per-token grace-window evaluations - owner: Console team (contact: Sofia Martinez) - estimate: 3
ENG-66011.8: Communicate to customers via status.redwood.ai about improved Retry headers and guidance for client SDKs about respecting Retry-After - owner: GTM - estimate: 1
success_criteria: No recurrence of shard-local 429 spikes caused by TTL unit mismatch in next 3 months
Per-route Retry-After-less 429s metric available and alerting rule defined (alert fires when > 1% sustained above baseline for 15 minutes)
Canary rollout pattern prevents global impact: automatic rollback triggers validated in testbed
Client SDKs adopted Retry-After handling in next minor release (tracked with SDK owners)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Unit + integration tests merged to main
Stage 1: Deploy fix to canary pool (2 shards) with grace-window metrics enabled
Stage 2: Monitor canary for 60m; if stable promote to 30% of shards; if stable after 3 hours promote to 100%
Stage 3: Enable transparent Retry headers behind feature flag; coordinate SDK rollouts over 2 weeks
Rollback criteria: 429 rate increase > 3% or SLO latency increase > 10% in any deployment window
post_deploy_checks: Verify 'grace_window_mismatch' is zero or within expected noise after full deploy
Confirm Retry-After and X-Redwood-Retryable headers are present for quota-failures in test requests
Run synthetic traffic mix (prefix-heavy, bursty renewals) to validate no shard-local surge

notes: This incident highlights the risk of silent unit/serialization changes crossing service boundaries; enforce stricter contract tests between auth-service and gateway for TTL/grace-window values.
Recommend adding a pre-merge contract check in CI that runs small contract-tests between services for critical numeric units (seconds vs ms)
